levels.title: Build Better Keywords
tips: Start broad, then narrow with AND.
Use OR to include synonyms.
Truncate with * to include variant endings (e.g., psycholog*).
Avoid natural language—think in concepts & synonyms.

prompts.topic: How did the treatment of mental illness change from the early 1900s to the late 1900s?
good_queries: "mental illness" AND treatment AND (asylum OR institutionalization) AND (deinstitutionalization OR "community care") AND ("1900s" OR "20th century")

prompts.topic: Impact of social media on adolescent sleep quality.
good_queries: "social media" AND adolescen* AND (sleep AND (quality OR duration))

prompts.topic: Effects of microplastics on marine invertebrates.
good_queries: microplastic* AND marine AND invertebrate* AND (toxic* OR ingestion)
"academic libraries" AND ("student parents" OR caregivers) AND (services OR support OR policies)

levels.title: Boolean Flight Plan
tips: AND narrows, OR broadens, NOT excludes.
Group synonyms with ( ) to control logic.
Put phrases in "quotes" to keep words together.

questions.stem: You need articles on college athletes and mental health, but not about professional leagues.
Broaden results about renewable energy cars: electric OR hybrid, but avoid motorcycles.
questions.answer: (electric OR hybrid) AND cars NOT motorcycles

questions.stem: Find items on climate change risk assessment, grouping synonyms.
questions.answer: "climate change" AND (risk OR hazard) AND assessment

questions.stem: Search for virtual reality in nursing education, excluding K-12.
questions.answer: "virtual reality" AND nursing AND education NOT K-12

levels.title: Sort the Sources
tips: Primary sources = original, first-hand (e.g., diaries, datasets).
Secondary = analysis/commentary about primary sources.
Scholarly vs. Popular: peer review, citations, formal tone vs. accessible, ads.

cards.text: A 1968 patient diary from a state hospital.
A meta-analysis of clinical trials in The Lancet.
A New York Times article on community mental health centers.
A book chapter interpreting WWII letters.
Peer-reviewed article reporting new field data.
TikTok explainer with citations in description.

levels.title: Database Matchmaking
tips: JSTOR: humanities, older coverage, stable PDFs; great for phrase search & date filters.
PubMed: biomedical/health; MeSH terms help.
PsycINFO: psychology/behavior, strong subject indexing.
Primo VE: books, media, many databases at once; use Advanced Search fields.

pairs.topic: Find if Lewis owns 'Phenomenology of Perception'
History of printing in Renaissance Italy

levels.title: CRAAP/RADAR Check
tips: Currency: is it up-to-date for the field?
Relevance/Authority: audience and author credentials.
Accuracy/Purpose: evidence, citations, bias disclaimers.

items.prompt: A blog post (2021) by a PhD sleep researcher summarizing their peer-reviewed study; cites the journal article; no ads.
items.why: Clear credentials, citations, and low bias indicators.

items.prompt: A site selling supplements claims 'microplastics cure!' with no citations; heavy product links.
items.why: Commercial bias, extraordinary claim without evidence.

items.prompt: A 1994 pop-magazine piece predicting the internet will end libraries by 2000.
Peer-reviewed article in 2019 reporting methods and data.
University repository preprint (2024) with references and author ORCIDs.
items.why: Scholarly context and traceable authorship add credibility.

levels.title: Lightning Round
tips: Peer-review signals: 'Received/Accepted' dates, DOI, references.
Citation basics: author, title, source, year; permalinks/DOIs preferred.
Broken links? Use the library link resolver or Primo 'Find It'.

signals.q: Which is a strong sign of peer review?
signals.why: DOIs and reference lists are common in scholarly articles.

signals.q: Best element to copy for a citation?
choices: The URL bar copy of a long session link
signals.why: Permalinks/DOIs are stable; session URLs break.

signals.q: You find a 404 on a scholarly article link. First move?
choices: Try Primo 'Find It' or the journal title search
signals.why: Link resolvers/journal search often locate full text.

signals.q: In JSTOR, which tactic narrows precisely?
signals.why: Quoted phrases reduce noise by keeping terms together.
